articles.title: How Naomi Osaka transformed her tennis success into a $120 multimillion-dollar business empire
articles.summary: International Sports News: Naomi Osaka’s success cannot be measured by trophies alone. The four-time Grand Slam champion has turned her tennis fame into a much broader business .
articles.body: Naomi Osaka’s success cannot be measured by trophies alone. The four-time Grand Slam champion has turned her tennis fame into a much broader business empire, with major deals in fashion, sportswear and luxury goods alongside investments in companies she helped build. Her financial story shows how modern athletes can create wealth long after the applause from the court fades.Naomi Osaka net worth and tennis earningsEstimates place Naomi Osaka’s net worth between $45 million and $60 million, while broader assessments of her brand and business interests have put her overall economic value closer to $120 million. Those figures vary because private investments, equity holdings and future business potential are difficult to value precisely.What is clearer is where much of her wealth comes from.Osaka has earned more than $25 million in career prize money on the WTA Tour. Her four Grand Slam singles victories played a major role in building those earnings, with each major title bringing significant prize money and greater global exposure.Yet tournament checks tell only part of the story.Osaka became one of tennis’ most marketable stars at a remarkably young age. Her appeal stretches across sport, fashion and popular culture, allowing her to work with companies that want to reach audiences far beyond traditional tennis fans.That commercial reach has become a major part of her financial success.Naomi Osaka endorsements and business venturesMajor brand partnerships have helped Osaka build an income stream that does not depend on how she performs in a particular tournament.Nike became one of her most prominent partners after the two entered a long-term apparel agreement in 2019. Her portfolio also expanded into luxury fashion and watches, including partnerships with Louis Vuitton and TAG Heuer. These relationships placed Osaka alongside some of the world's biggest names in fashion and luxury.Her business interests go further.Osaka has invested in ventures where she can hold an ownership stake rather than simply receive payment for promoting a product. That distinction can matter enormously over time. An endorsement typically provides income for a defined partnership, while equity can potentially increase in value as a company grows.One of her notable ventures is KINLÒ, a skincare brand created with the needs of melanated skin in mind. She also co-founded Hana Kuma, a media company focused on storytelling and culturally significant projects.Her interest in sports extends into representation as well. Through Evolve, Osaka has entered the sports management space, giving her a role in helping other athletes navigate their careers.The strategy creates something larger than a collection of endorsement deals. It gives Osaka exposure to several industries while allowing her to develop assets that can remain valuable beyond her playing career.That may ultimately prove to be one of the most important parts of her financial journey.Osaka's career illustrates a major shift in professional sports. Athletes are no longer limited to earning money from competition and advertisements. The most successful can become investors, founders and business owners in their own right.Her four Grand Slam titles gave Naomi Osaka a global platform. Her business decisions have helped turn that platform into something much bigger.For Osaka, the tennis court remains central to her identity, but it is no longer the only place where her career creates value.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pahokee football stuns Royal Palm on 75-yard 'Hail Mary' touchdown
articles.summary: Pahokee escaped upset with a miraculous 75-yard touchdown on the final play, stunning Royal Palm Beach.
articles.body:
ROYAL PALM BEACH — Corian Davis might want to get comfortable in the spotlight because his name is going to be everywhere this week.

Pahokee 's cornerback-turned-receiver delivered the play of the week, and perhaps the play of the year, Friday night with a stunning 75-yard 'Hail Mary' touchdown as time expired to lift the Blue Devils to a 16-14 victory over Royal Palm Beach.

Facing an upset loss, Pahokee stood at its own 25-yard line with 10.1 seconds remaining. Quarterback Braylon Peterson started a desperate final play, lateraling to Uzarus Boswell, who launched a pass downfield to Davis.

Davis hauled in the pass, slipped through would-be tacklers and zigzagged across the field before breaking free for the winning score.

By the time he crossed the goal line, the clock had long since hit triple zeroes, triggering a wild celebration from the Pahokee sideline and cementing the play's place among the most memorable moments in the program's storied history.

"That was electrifying, man," Pahokee coach Carlos Lammons said. "I've been playing ball for a while. Played in college, played in bowl games, high school, state championships, four in a row. Man, I don't think I've ever been a part of a play of that magnitude. And for it to go down like that, the kid had to go over top of two people, break two tackles, and sprint another 40 yards. Man, that was amazing."

"I think it can be," Lammons said. "I think it will be. I think it should be."

How a wild ending helped Pahokee avoid upset

Zyon Gilbert got the scoring started on defense for Pahokee, returning an interception for a touchdown in the first quarter to stake the Blue Devils to a 7-0 advantage.

That was the type of start many expected. And when Pahokee nearly scored again, fumbling inside Royal Palm Beach's 10 yard line, it was seen as a hiccup.

With Royal Palm fielding a team replacing its quarterback and lead running back from 2025 and with turnover on its defensive side of the roster, not many knew what to expect.

But the Wildcats responded with a touchdown pass to Demetrius Gibson and began to take control of the momentum, and suddenly the game very much reflected the full-moon sky hovering above.

The Wildcats would scored once more on a 58-yard punt return for a touchdown by Demetrice Rolle — and for a time, that appeared destine to be the play of the game.

Pahokee added a field goal, but was unable to put together a go-ahead drive as the clock ticked down late into the fourth quarter.

The Blue Devils got one more shot with fewer than 40 seconds left inside their own 10 yard line.

An incomplete pass. A desperate run by Peterson. Still, it looked like the story of Friday's game had been written.

Peterson, Boswell, and Davis rewrote it in a moment, turning the game on its side in a moment of both jubilation and heartbreak, an epitome of Friday Night Lights.

"To be honest, I really can't tell you what went on," Davis said. "All I can tell you that the quarterback made a good throw. There wasn't really that much time left on the bar. So somebody had to make a big play and I made that big play. And we're gonna keep on doing it the whole year, the whole season."

"My team they stayed in the game," he continued. "They didn't give up. We bent, but we ain't break."

Not bad for Corian Davis' first week on offense

The junior cornerback is accustomed to being a difference-maker on defense, but this was a new twist.

Corian Davis took reps on the offensive side of the ball for the first time this week. And yet, with the game on the line, Davis was always the intended receiver in the play drawn up by the coaches.

"We knew coming in this week that we're gonna need an extra playmaker on offense," Lammons said. "This guy is a playmaker. When we need him, we know where to bring him."

Not a bad start on offense. Not bad at all.

Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at apeterman@usatodayco.com.

articles.title: Tarik Skubal Responds to Mixed Reception From Tigers Fans
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal had a hilarious response when asked whether Detroit Tigers fans booed him during his emotional return to Comerica Park.
articles.body:
He just isn't quite sure what everyone was saying.

The former Detroit Tigers ace made his highly anticipated return to Comerica Park on Friday night, this time wearing a Los Angeles Dodgers uniform. Skubal received plenty of cheers prior to the start of the game, but there were certainly plenty of boos once he took the mound against his former team.

After the game, Skubal was asked the obvious question.

His answer was about as perfect as it gets.

"You know with the last name Skoob, you don't know if they are boos or they're cheering for you and I gotta assume they were cheering for me," Skubal said. "That's all I gotta say about that"

Tarik Skubal's Emotional Return to Detroit

The reception had been one of the biggest storylines surrounding Skubal's return ever since it became clear his spot in the Dodgers rotation would bring him back to Detroit less than a month after the trade.

Before the game, the Tigers honored Skubal with a video tribute as he walked back from the bullpen . Skubal appeared emotional during the moment as fans throughout Comerica Park stood and applauded.

That came after Skubal had already admitted he expected his return to Detroit to be emotional .

Once Skubal took the mound, however, the reception became a little more complicated.

MLB reported that there were plenty of boos mixed with calls of "Skooooob" when the left-hander took the mound.

Which, as Skubal pointed out afterward, creates a pretty convenient loophole.

Skubal has apparently decided to believe Option B.

Whatever fans were yelling, Skubal did not let it bother him.

He held Detroit to one run on four hits over six innings, striking out seven without issuing a walk. He threw only 83 pitches, 56 for strikes, before Dodgers manager Dave Roberts ended his night.

Skubal appeared visibly unhappy when Roberts informed him after the sixth inning that he was finished, but his work was done.

Los Angeles eventually escaped Comerica Park with a 2-1 victory, while Detroit fell to 62-72. Skubal's reception was described as mostly cheers with a smattering of boos during his first appearance at Comerica Park as a visiting player.

There had been plenty of debate leading into Friday about how Tigers fans would treat their former ace.

Skubal found an easier way to settle it.

articles.title: No letdown for Brick Memorial football with new QB, new coach in opening win vs. Wall
articles.summary: The shoes Brick Memorial senior quarterback Tyler Pierce has to fill this season are gigantic. But Pierce showed the moment was not too big.
articles.body:
BRICK - The shoes Brick Memorial senior quarterback Tyler Pierce has to fill this season are gigantic

But, Friday night, Pierce showed the moment was not too big for him as he threw two touchdown passes and ran for another to lead defending NJSIAA Central Group 4 champion Mustangs to a resounding 28-3 win over Wall in a season-opening nondivisional game at DiFabio Field and James Mahoney's first game as a head coach.

Pierce, was 12-for-15 for 108 yards with an interception on a tipped pass and TD passes of 3 yards to senior running back Colin Schoellkopf and 5 yards to his twin brother Casey He ran for 80 yards, including a 30-yard TD run for Brick Memorial's first TD.

Brick Memorial Football handles Wall 28-3 in Season Opener

The Mustangs scored on their first four possessions and had drives of 93 yards in 11 plays that led to Shawn Fowler's 6-yard TD on a fourth-and-2 and 73 yards in 13 plays that took up the first 9:19 of the third quarter and concluded with Pierce's TD to his brother.

The son of former Brick Memorial quarterback and 1997 graduate Jeff Pierce is taking the place of Jason Lajara, who graduated in June after setting numerous school records.

"It's big shoes to fill, but that's why I train,'' the soft-spoken Pierce said. "That's what I'm here for.''

Fowler, a senior wide receiver/Wildcat quarterback/defensive back said the Mustangs' players were not worried about whether Pierce was up to the job.

"For the past 3 years, he's been that guy who texted Mahoney (Mahoney was the Mustangs' offensive coordinator the last several years before becoming head coach after Walt Currie resigned last December after 19 seasons as the Mustangs' head coach) asking for film during lunch,'' Fowler said. "He's going to grind in the weight room. That's the kind of person he is.''

It was not only Lajara, Brick Memorial has had to replace. It has to replace three other Asbury Park Press First Team All-Shore players in linebacker Trey Tallmadge, wide receiver Nyzier Matthews and running back Na'zeer Whittaker.

"Tyler's been there. It's not like he's been a secret. He was there practicing with us,'' Fowler said. "He just took that experience from learning from Jason Lajara and translated it to the game.''

Work ethic showed Pierce had what it took to be the starter.

Mahoney said he saw the potential Pierce last winter during basketball season when Pierce became one of the team's starters. Mahoney is an assistant coach in basketball to head coach Keith Farr. Farr is Brick Memorial's wide receivers coach.

"Tyler works real hard in the weight room,'' Mahoney said. "He's super strong. He's competitive. In the middle of last year, nobody knew who was going to be the quarterback this year. It could have been Fowler. It could have been Livio (senior tight end Joe Livio) and all of the sudden Tyler started to emerge. He became Jason Lajara's shadow in the offseason, doing everything he did, going to camps, getting better.

"Tyler doesn't care about anything, but winning and doing the best he can for his team.

Pierce has come a long way after not starting on the freshman team in 2024.

"Tyler Pierce is what we call a Brick Memorial program kid,'' Mahoney said. "He stuck it out and did everything he was told to do. I'm just super proud of him.''

Pierce showed his poise throughout the game.

Pierce's TD run came on a second-and-10 and capped a 55-yard, six-play drive after Wall had taken a 3-0 lead on a 27-yard field goal by Kai Smith.

"I saw the end go out on Colin (Schoellkopf) so I pulled it and ran. Joe (Livio) had a good block for me. Shawn (Fowler) had a good block for me,'' Pierce said.

Pierce's legs bailed Brick Memorial out of a difficult spot on its second possession when he scrambled up the middle for 42 yards on a third-and-12 from the Mustangs' 5.

"We put our quarterback in stressful situations in practice so when the game's come, it seems a little slower,'' Mahoney said. "Ty's the type of kid where if you tell him something, he's going to do it. ''

Pierce also got a baptism by fire last year in Brick Memorial's second game when he was thrust into the lineup of the second game of the season against then defending Group 2 champion Rumson-Fair Haven because Lajara was sidelined with an illness and Tallmadge, the backup. sustained an injury.

He then got snaps in the Mustangs' regular season win over Brick Township and playoff wins over Marlboro and Steinert.

"Starting this summer, he took this team and made it his.'' Mahoney said.

articles.summary: The Red Sox reportedly are close to welcoming Roman Anthony and Trevor Story back after their offense was shut out for the second consecutive game.
articles.body:
The Roman Anthony and Trevor Story waiting game might finally be approaching its conclusion. Anthony and Story reportedly have completed their rehab assignments with Triple-A Worcester and are expected to join the Boston Red Sox in New York, according to MLB reporter Francys Romero.

Romero added that either player could be activated Saturday or Sunday during Boston's four-game series against the Yankees.

That leaves some mystery surrounding the exact timing of their returns. Neither player was with the Red Sox for Friday night's series opener despite growing speculation that at least Anthony might rejoin the club in the Bronx.

Anthony instead reported to Polar Park on Friday after going 2-for-4 with an RBI double and a single Thursday. He has hit .304 with two home runs during rehab stops with Double-A Portland and Worcester.

Now, it appears his rehab work is complete.

The same reportedly is true for Story, giving Boston a chance to add two important hitters before the weekend concludes.

Red Sox Offense Desperately Needs Reinforcements

The timing could not be better for the Red Sox.

Boston suffered a 1-0 loss to the Yankees on Friday, marking its second consecutive shutout. The Red Sox have gone 18 straight innings without scoring a run and wasted an excellent performance from Patrick Sandoval in the series opener. Boston collected five hits and drew six walks against New York but finished 0-for-9 with runners in scoring position. The Red Sox left 10 runners on base and failed to take advantage of five walks from Yankees starter Cam Schlittler.

Paul Goldschmidt's third-inning solo home run accounted for the game's only scoring.

The loss dropped Boston three games behind New York in the American League East and seven games behind the division-leading Tampa Bay Rays. The Red Sox and Yankees will play a doubleheader Saturday, creating a possible opportunity for Anthony or Story to make an immediate impact.

Anthony would add another dangerous left-handed hitter to the lineup. Story would provide a proven bat while restoring Boston's regular presence at shortstop.

The Red Sox have not officially announced when either player will be activated, so the mystery is not completely over.

The finish line, however, finally appears to be in sight. After consecutive nights without a run, Boston could not ask for the offensive help to arrive at a better time.

articles.title: Giants' Willy Adames seeks late September return, improvement in 2027
articles.summary: San Francisco Giants shortstop Willy Adames, out with an elbow sprain, hopes to return for a few at-bats next month but is focused on improving his overall g...
articles.body:
Of course Willy Adames wants to play again this season if he's able to after he recovers from a left elbow sprain, the question almost doesn't even have to be asked. But much as the San Francisco Giants shortstop loves to make every start, he knows in this case it might not be the wisest course of action.

Adames got a platelet-rich plasma injection Thursday evening and will be held back from activity for a few days, but the recovery timeline is three to four weeks. That makes a return in the last week of the season possible. Maybe. A couple of at-bats before the season ends would be ideal, he said.

"I'm hoping that I can play in the last week - I don't know how many days we're going to have," Adames said. "But if I'm not 100%, I don't think I'm going to push it. It would be different if we were in a different position, but even though I want to be out there every day, I have to feel 100%."

Adames was injured in a play at the plate last Sunday in Boston when catcher Connor Wong 's knee connected with his arm.

"I didn't really feel when his knee hit me, I just kind of felt pain when I slid," Adames said. "I knew there was something in there, but I didn't know it was like that - I thought maybe a few days (of rest) and it would have been fine, but it was worse than what I thought."

Adames' back, which has bothered him much of the season, has calmed down, but there's no doubt that some extended time off would also help ensure the back is no longer a problem next year. And like the rest of the team, Adames is all about next year - he had a season he called "disappointing" on both sides of the ball.

Adames is hitting .230 with 21 homers and his 62 runs are second most on the team; his defense, in part because of his back, was poor, tied for the worst Outs Above Average in the majors, at -17 along with a -5 Defensive Runs Saved according to the Fielding Bible.

Next year, he must be healthy, for starters. What else does he need to do differently?

"Everything," Adames said. "It felt like I couldn't get it right this year, on defense or offense. So I'll work on reevaluating what I was doing this year and then focus on all the points that I have to adjust and go about it in the offseason."

Adames has a coach he works with every winter in the Dominican Republic, Angel Gonzalez, who will help.

"He always brings me back to my roots and where I have to go when I'm not doing well," Adames said. "We always work and make an adjustment so whatever I was doing wrong that year I can come back the next year and do my thing."

Pitching possibilities: Left-hander Matt "Tugboat" Wilkinson and right-hander Yunior Marte are on hand but were not active for Friday's game. Wilkinson is likely to be the 27th player for Saturday's doubleheader against Arizona , and Marte could be an addition depending on how Friday night's game goes. If the bullpen isn't overtaxed, one of the games might be a bullpen game.

Marte, like Jonah Cox, would be coming straight from Double-A Richmond, where he had a 3.92 ERA and 72 strikeouts in 64⅓ innings in 13 starts. The 23-year-old was obtained from the Royals for Mike Yastrzemski last year.

Briefly: Marcelo Mayer is out of his walking boot and could be an option for the Giants at some point soon; manager Tony Vitello said the infielder will increase his activity over the next couple of days. Another rehab assignment might be necessary before he makes his Giants debut but it certainly looks more likely that will happen next month. … Sharks stars Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith took batting practice with the Giants for the second year in a row, and this time Smith, who came close last year, went deep.

articles.title: WATCH: Tacario Davis gets his first NFL interception
articles.summary: The rookie was Johnny on the spot.
articles.body:
Rookie cornerback Tacario Davis was taken in the third round of the NFL Draft this season. It was a bit earlier than some experts anticipated, but the measurables were simply so rare to find.

At 6'4 and a hair under 195 lbs., you simply do not find guys at that size who can play corner every year, and it's something the Cincinnati Bengals needed more of.

So, it's good to see he does have some pretty good ball skills, which we saw in Friday's preseason finale vs. the Philadelphia Eagles , turning a pass that went through the receiver's hands into an interception.

This play is exactly what you want to see from your corners. Making a play on the ball in a split second that shouldn't be there. He even had a little wiggle there on the return.

This also came after Davis had a beautiful deflection on the first drive of the game. The commentators said he is playing in this game because the coaches want to see him get more reps. They plan on deploying him in certain packages to use his size on bigger receivers.

For those that remember Tre Flowers who had a short stint with the team during their run to the Super Bowl. He was used against the talented tight ends that are such matchup nightmares for defenses. Davis may be used in a similar fashion early in his career.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. shows he belongs with Giants in preseason finale
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. has done all he can to earn a roster spot with the NY Giants. Now comes the final decision, which is out of his hands.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD - Odell Beckham Jr. has done all he can, fighting for a roster spot with the New York Giants this summer the way an undrafted rookie would.

There's no denying what represents to this franchise, but for the purposes of his quest to earn his place on this team - not based on the past, but the present and future - Beckham can say he left no doubt regarding what he wants, what he is willing to do to accomplish that and where he wants to be following Friday's 23-6 victory over the Jets in the preseason finale at MetLife Stadium.

Now the Giants will have to decide if Beckham has done enough to survive Sunday's 6 p.m. NFL-mandated deadline for teams to pare their rosters to 53. At this point, it'd be a big surprise if Beckham was not here when the Giants hit the practice field next week to begin preparing for their Sept. 13 season opener against the Dallas Cowboys.

"It would mean everything. It would be my dream," Beckham told NBC's Bruce Beck, who asked what it would mean to play for the Giants again during the TV broadcast. "This is where I started. There's no place I wanna give my whole heart to - more than anything else in the world - it's this place right here."

Giants vs Jets photos from final preseason game at MetLife Stadium

It's not as if Beckham was taking anything for granted in his quest to make the team and complete this next chapter of his improbable comeback with the New York Giants , because he almost certainly was not.

But that message from John Harbaugh on June 1 when Beckham's Big Blue return became official still resonates: "You can't be just OK. You're Odell Beckham."

That's what Harbaugh told him nearly three months ago, appealing to the greater sense of responsibility Beckham feels when it comes to living up to the legacy that remains incomplete.

Against the Jets, Beckham had three catches for 53 yards and came within inches of hauling in what would have been an old school OBJ diving catch on a deep seam pass from Jameis Winston. The 33-year-old former Pro Bowler left a pair of Jets defenders in his wake, but Winston's throw did not hit him in stride; the ball was just beyond his reach, and despite Beckham's fully extended attempt, the football just slipped off his fingertips.

This was a chance to rewrite the next chapter of this comeback story, and to this point, after an entire season away from the game, Beckham has defied odds that were against him given the circumstances.

This was always about getting another chance to say thank you to a fan base, loyal and passionate about one of the most popular and polarizing players of a generation. Because of that, Beckham has been living in two football worlds and his current place with the Giants had very little to do with his spectacular previous life with Big Blue.

Beckham is doing what the Giants have asked him to do, and that's make the most of his chances. He is winning his routes. He is finishing his blocks, playing in the second halves of preseason games because that's how bad he wants this to work.

Much of Beckham's skill set is perceived to be finesse and outrageous physical talent. He's shown grit and toughness, fighting through grueling Harbaugh practices while running with quarterback Brandon Allen before Winston and Dart had the chance to even glance his way.

The perfect ending for Beckham's Giants comeback would not be an ending at all. It's all about earning the new beginning here that he so desperately wanted, and with Calvin Austin lost for the season with a torn ACL, the path to the 53-man roster is a lot clearer than it was earlier this week.

Perhaps it should be no surprise that, once this team really needed Beckham to step up, challenging him to take it to another level, he's turned on a part of his game so many predicted would never resurface again.

"I think Odell's had a good camp. I would say his best week of camp has come this week," Harbaugh said. "He's looked good and made numerous plays, and just like you saw, even [Wednesday], made numerous plays, so he's doing well."

Domin(automat)ic Zvada. Good again, this time from 46. The undrafted rookie is seemingly pulling away from Ben Sauls in the kicking competition, if he had not put it away already. He was 3-for-3 on field goals, including a 53-yarder that he made with plenty of room, and was good on a pair of point-after touchdowns, too.

articles.title: Texans drop final preseason game to Panthers 16-13
articles.summary: The preseason is finally over, long live the regular season!
articles.body:
If you sat down to watch the third Texans' preseason game and watched the entire thing, you get nothing but respect from me. Because this game was just difficult to watch. No starters played, as was expected because who wants to put starters at risk for a meaningless game, but there were things that we could learn from the game.

First of all, the offensive line cannot afford a single injury this season. Not a one. Because the depth behind the Texans line is upsetting. The backups, in the first drive of the game, surrendered two sacks of Davis Mills. That was the opening drive when our backups should have been up for the game getting completely pants'd by future grocery stockers.

While it might not be enough to get him a spot on the roster, Sabastian Harsh had the game of his life, racking up three tackles, a sack, and a pass deflection on the day. He might make the practice squad based on that performance.

Beyond that, it was a snooze for most of the game. Neither team scored a touchdown until late in the fourth quarter of the game. It was a bad, boring game that we had to get through to watch real football. And now we are clear for the regular season.

The Houston Texans' season starts Sunday September 6 at noon CDT against the Buffalo Bills. We'll see you then!

articles.title: Final Score: Giants backups crush Jets backups in preseason finale
articles.summary: Jets manhandled by cross town rivals
articles.body:
In the New York Jets' third and final preseason game of 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets were defeated by the New York Giants, 23 – 6.

The Jets opened on defense and on third down they intercepted Jameis Winston. That set them up with first and ten at the Giants 36. The Jets proceeded to run a 10 play drive that ended with a short Chip Trayanum touchdown run. No passes were thrown in the drive. Jason Sanders missed the extra point to make the score Jets 6, Giants 0.

The Giants proceeded to put together a long drive that ended when the Jets forced a fumble by old friend Braxton Berrios into their own end zone for a touchback. The turnovers are flowing for the Jets this preseason.

Late in the first quarter the Giants took advantage of a short field to go on a drive culminating in a Tyrone Tracy touchdown run and a 7 – 6 Giants lead. The first quarter ended a few seconds later with the score still 7 – 6.

A few plays into the second quarter Cade Klubnick threw a terrible pass into tight coverage that was picked off by the Giants. The Giants then put together a long drive that bogged down inside the Jets five yard line. They converted on a chip shot field goal to take a 10 – 6 lead with less than three minutes left in the half. Neither team got much going on offense the last few minutes and the half ended with the score still Giants 10, Jets 6.

The Jets opened the third quarter on offense. Bailey Zappe took over for Cade Klubnik at quarterback and promptly led the team on a scintillating three and out. The Giants offensive scrubs took over and put together a short drive ending in a 53 yard field goal and a 13 – 6 Giants lead midway through the third quarter.

Zappe took over on offense and engineered a thrilling three and out as he made his case to be cut on Sunday.

Legendary quarterback Jake Haener took over for the Giants and led them on a long drive. The third quarter ended with the score still Giants 13, Jets 6, but the Giants were lining up for a field goal attempt. On the first play of the fourth quarter the Giants hit on a 46 yard field goal as the Giants took a 16 -6 lead to open the fourth quarter.

Bailey Zappe proceeded to lead the Jets on a stirring three and out as he continued to impress.

Jake The Legend Haener then led the Giants on a swift drive resulting in a touchdown on a 37 yard pass to old friend Xavier Gipson as the Giants piled on with 23 unanswered points. The score was Giants 23, Jets 6 with 10:30 left in the game.

Midway through the fourth quarter the Jets turned to Brady Cook at quarterback. Cook led the Jets on a short drive ending in a missed 54 yard field goal by Jason Sanders, who had a rough night and may have played himself off the team.

Jake The Goat Haener and the Giants then closed out the game with a long drive to the Jets one yard line before taking a knee on the last three plays of the game.

Final score: Giants 23, Jets 6. The loss brought the Jets' preseason record to 1-2. The score doesn't really matter. The record doesn't really matter. The most important development in the game were injuries to Anez Cooper, Chip Trayanum, Dominic Richardson and Joseph Ossai. We'll see if these end up being injuries that threaten to keep these players out for an extended period of time. Now the Jets move on to getting their roster down to 53 players by 6:00 P.M. EDT on Sunday. They then begin preparations for their opening day game against the Tennessee Titans on September 13.

articles.title: Washington legend describes Commanders' performance in one word
articles.summary: Washington legend London Fletcher had one word to describe the Commanders' performance in preseason loss to Ravens.
articles.body:
Was that one of the worst preseason performances you've ever seen? The Washington Commanders were slow, lifeless, and got drilled by the Ravens 41-3 in Baltimore on Friday.

With about eight roster spots up for grabs, how is it that the Commanders came so ill-prepared? Yes, I get that they declared 41 players out for the game in the hours before kickoff. But what about the other 49 guys who were playing, wearing burgundy and gold?

From the first snap, the Commanders were a step slow, getting blown off the ball, couldn't get the Ravens offense off the field, and by halftime (30 minutes in), the Commanders offense had produced only a first down. One half of football and one first down by your offense?

Even former Commanders receiver Chris Moore played much better in a Ravens uniform. Moore caught three passes in the opening drive, including a difficult touchdown grab down the right sideline.

It didn't get any better in the third quarter. When that quarter ended, the Ravens had produced 24 first downs, while Washington had only three. As a result, the Commanders trailed 34-3. Watching the Ravens offense do what they wanted on the Commanders defense, former Washington Redskins linebacker London Fletcher, a part of the Commanders radio broadcast team, had enough. "This is gross right now, quite frankly," said Fletcher.

Fletcher was frank; he was also correct. Fletcher is hired by the Commanders to work the broadcast, to provide commentary. Would most announcers say something so blunt as calling the Commanders' performance "gross?" Of course they wouldn't. But Fletcher had a very high standard for what a player is supposed to do and how much effort he is supposed to exert. It's what made him a great NFL linebacker. So he called out the Commanders... "gross."

How must new offensive coordinator David Blough feel? His offensive line again produced little to nothing on Friday. Then the Commanders' third-down offense was absolutely impotent, going 0-11. No, that is not a misprint, 0-11. They did get one late, making it 1-12.

Sorry to all the Washington fans who planned the trip, paid for a ticket, and drove to Baltimore to show support for your team. But your team, for some reason(s), simply didn't come prepared mentally. We know this because there was no fire; there was little intensity. Third-year safety Tyler Owens seriously appeared to be the only exception. He had two very intense hits, and they stood out in dark contrast to the rest of the team's effort on Friday.

For a team with so many questions coming into this game, they certainly didn't answer any positively.

articles.title: NFL Legend Ryan Fitzpatrick’s Harsh Deshaun Watson Reality Check Gives Shedeur Sanders Fans Hope
articles.summary: Deshaun Watson has the starting job in Cleveland Browns, but the whispers about his job security have not stopped. Fresh off a 31-7 blowout loss to the Buffa...
articles.body:
Deshaun Watson has the starting job in Cleveland Browns , but the whispers about his job security have not stopped. Fresh off a 31-7 blowout loss to the Buffalo Bills in the preseason, where Shedeur Sanders looked sharper in his snaps, the Browns quarterback room remains the most scrutinized story in football.

Now a former NFL passer turned broadcaster has offered a blunt forecast that Cleveland fans will not forget anytime soon.

Ryan Fitzpatrick Sees Shedeur Sanders Taking Over Once Deshaun Watson Stumbles

The comments came during a Prime Video segment, where Fitzpatrick and longtime broadcast partner Kirk Herbstreit broke down Cleveland's messy quarterback situation. Herbstreit asked directly whether Fitzpatrick believed the veteran signal caller was destined to lose the job. Fitzpatrick did not hesitate.

"Once he fails, Shedeur is going to jump into this thing, and he's going to be the guy. And this city is going to be behind him." Fitzpatrick said on-air.

Herbstreit pressed further, asking if Fitzpatrick truly expected Watson to come up short. Fitzpatrick's response left little room for interpretation, insisting the outcome felt inevitable rather than merely possible.

The prediction lands at a strange moment for the Browns. Head coach Todd Monken handed Watson the Week 1 job over Sanders after training camp, a decision that drew immediate backlash from a fanbase already weary of Watson's play and his contract.

Sanders, meanwhile, has quietly built momentum. He already has a bold starting quarterback prediction from Gerald McCoy, and teammates like Jerry Jeudy have publicly backed him to eventually take over.

Watson's Rocky Preseason Keeps Fueling The Debate

Watson's grip on the job took another hit after Cleveland's 31-7 preseason loss to the Bills on August 22. He completed just 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards and an interception, and fans at Huntington Bank Field booed him loudly throughout. Watson called the reaction personal in his postgame press conference.

"It's a little bit personal. It's a disrespectful thing," Watson said afterward.

The comments drew sharp criticism from media members who felt Watson was blaming supporters instead of his own performance.

Sanders, by contrast, has vowed to change the franchise's quarterback history , and that contrast is exactly why Fitzpatrick's prediction spread so quickly.

Watson remains Cleveland's starter heading into the regular season, but the margin for error looks razor thin. The Browns open the year on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars on September 13, a fresh test for a quarterback room still searching for stability.

articles.title: Yankees nip rival Red Sox 1-0 in series opener behind Goldschmidt, Bellinger and Schlittler
articles.summary: Paul Goldschmidt homered, left fielder Cody Bellinger threw out the potential tying run at home plate to end the seventh inning and the New York Yankees edge...
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Paul Goldschmidt homered, left fielder Cody Bellinger threw out the potential tying run at home plate to end the seventh inning and the New York Yankees edged the Boston Red Sox 1-0 on Friday night in the opener of a pivotal four-game series.

Cam Schlittler (12-6) shut down his hometown team again, striking out eight in 5 2/3 innings of two-hit ball. The right-hander from Walpole, Massachusetts overcame five walks, which matched a career high, as the Red Sox went 1 for 7 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 overall.

They also cost themselves with a terrible baserunning blunder by Ceddanne Rafaela, who got doubled off first as the trail runner when Wilyer Abreu lined out to center field — ending the fifth with cleanup batter Willson Contreras on deck.

New York remained four games behind first-place Tampa Bay in the AL East and moved three ahead of Boston in the race for the top American League wild-card and home-field advantage throughout a potential best-of-three playoff series between the longtime rivals.

Such a matchup would be a reprisal of last year, when Schlittler pitched a Game 3 gem as a rookie to send the Yankees on. Schlittler, who leads the AL with a 2.09 ERA this season, is 3-1 with a 0.56 ERA and 39 strikeouts in 32 1/3 innings over five career starts against Boston — including the postseason.

In a nip-and-tuck game with a playoff feel, Boston put runners at second and third with one out in the seventh when Rafaela singled and Abreu doubled on the first two pitches from reliever Paul Blackburn.

Contreras lofted a fly to left and Bellinger cut down Rafaela at the plate with a 99.7 mph throw.

Blackburn worked a 1-2-3 eighth and David Bednar pitched a perfect ninth for his 31st save.

With the Yankees facing a left-handed starter for the first time since Aug. 8 (excluding openers), Goldschmidt batted leadoff and launched a 430-foot homer to left off hard-luck loser Patrick Sandoval (1-3) in the third.

A day-night doubleheader Saturday to make up a June 6 rainout. Max Fried (4-4, 2.81 ERA) will come off the injured list to start the early game for the Yankees, with fellow left-hander Carlos Rodón (4-2, 3.15) taking the ball in the other. Rookie LHP Jake Bennett (8-6, 3.49) pitches the opener for the Red Sox, who had not announced a Game 2 starter.

articles.title: Shelby defense shining despite question mark entering 2026 season
articles.summary: After another dominant defensive performance, the Shelby Whippets' defense is again a major strength of the team.
articles.body:
LEXINGTON — Coming into the 2026 football season, there was a question mark around the Shelby Whippets' defense.

Replacing nine starters from a squad that allowed just 10.9 points per game and pitched four shutouts during a run to the Division IV state title appearance is enough to make anyone question the Whippets on that side of the ball.

After a 48-6 victory over Lexington on Friday, Aug. 28, which followed a 54-0 win over Madison in Week 1, the Whippets (2-0) defense has answered every question imaginable after not allowing a touchdown in the first two weeks of the season. Lexington's lone score came on a fumble return.

"We have had a lot of guys step up for us," Shelby senior linebacker Griffin Yeager said. "We have eight guys who rotate in on defense and what has helped us so much is our preparation each week. Our defensive coaches are great and challenge us to step up."

In the win over Lexington, Shelby allowed just 68 total yards of offense with just 14 through the air. They picked off two passes to give them seven total turnovers in two weeks. And they have done it with new faces everywhere they look.

Needless to say, Shelby coach Rob Mahaney is pleased with his defensive group.

"A ton," Mahaney said. "We came into the season wanting to play some faster guys in different positions and also challenge our two interior guys to play both ways and our kids have done a tremendous job of accepting those challenges. Our defensive philosophy hasn't changed – we ask them to do their jobs and play team football.

"As long as we continue to do that, we give ourselves a chance."

The offense was just as complementary in Week 2. Michael Shepherd completed 13-of-19 passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns while adding 19 yards and two scores on the ground. Gavin Baker ran for 104 yards on 11 carries with two scores and Luke Blevins added 55 rushing yards on just three carries. The Whippets ran for 178 yards.

"One of the things we wanted to focus on tonight was putting in plays where Michael didn't have to read people making them more straight runs instead of ROPs," Mahaney said. "The credit goes to the O-Line because we had holes to run through all game. Those five seniors controlled the line of scrimmage and when Gavin and Luke got their opportunities, they were great with the ball. They were explosive and found seams."

Brady Bowman, who had just two catches for 25 yards, was electric in the punt return game returning five punts for 90 yards and a TD of 54 yards.

"The awesome part about Brady is he was effective on defense, blocking in the run game on offense and returning punts," Mahaney said. "He impacted the game in multiple ways and what is special is he wasn't demanding the ball on offense. Such a great teammate who changed the game with his punt returns."

Conner Hartz and Branson Reed both added interceptions on defense while Yeager had a sack.

"Our coverage calls set us up amazingly well," Yeager said. "We prep with film all the time to the point we know what routes they are going to run. We know what is coming at us before the ball is even snapped."

Mix preparation with speed and you get a secondary that already has five interceptions and three defensive scores on the season.

"Speed really is a difference maker," Mahaney said. "When you can play fast and physical on defense, it creates a lot of pressure on the quarterback and forces some hurried throws that allow our skill guys to make plays. Ton of credit goes to our kids and our defensive staff."

It is the side of the ball that put the entire area on notice and is now looked at as an explanation mark and not a question. They hope to continue it next week at home against Bellevue.

"We play for each other, man," Yeager said. "We are taught to fly to the ball and fly around and make plays. That's just how it is at Shelby.

"It definitely gave us a chip on our shoulders. We were counted out as a defense. Everyone thought our offense was going to have to carry us and while it is doing great, our defense is playing very well."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo flicks game-winning goal to keep Al Nassr undefeated
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo flicked the ball in for his second goal since the World Cup to help Al Nassr remain undefeated in the Saudi Pro League season.
articles.body:
The Cristiano Ronaldo train keeps chugging along!

The Portuguese legend scored what ended up being the winning goal for Al Nassr on Friday, Aug. 28 in a match against Al Taawoun at Al-Awwal Park in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The goal came in the 50th minute after Al Nassr already answered Al Taawoun's first score of the match. The ball bounced off a falling Sadio Mané, and Mohamed Simakan kicked it toward the goal where Ronaldo was up close. He then flicked the ball into the net with his heel. To celebrate, the former Real Madrid star trotted toward the middle of the pitch with his hands up and flashed his signature grin.

The goal made the score 2-1, keeping Al Nassr undefeated with its fourth consecutive victory since the Saudi Pro League season kicked off earlier this month.

This was the five-time Ballon d'Or winner's second goal for Al Nassr this season. He scored his first goal since the 2026 World Cup in the 4-0 win over Al Riyadh a week earlier.

Ronaldo, 41, got married to his longtime partner , Georgina Rodríguez, days before the Saudi Pro League season started.

He scored three goals in this summer's World Cup , including his first in a knockout round . It was his sixth time in the tournament, which ties the record for most World Cups with Lionel Messi and Guillermo Ochoa.

Erling Haaland wasn't the only World Cup star to debut a new haircut when league play started. Ronaldo donned bleach blond hair when he first got back on the pitch for Al Nassr.

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan: Scaffolding returns to site of viral 'zombie-like' mural of The Rocket in Sheffield
articles.summary: Viral 30ft mural of Ronnie O'Sullivan in Sheffield sees scaffolding return to it after comical, negative reviews of Rocket's likeness; Artist Chris Ashmore: "I saw people saying it looks like Michael Jackson or a zombie. I've got thick skin, I'll be okay, but it didn't feel fair"
articles.body:
Sheffield artist Chris Ashmore created the 30ft mural at Spot On Snooker Club in the city's Langsett Road.

In a post from August 15, on his business Facebook page Creative Murals and Portraits UK, Mr Ashmore shared images of the mural which appeared to be nearly complete.

The artwork shows the seven-time world champion leaning down for a shot with a cue and rest and was revealed in full when the scaffolding came down recently.

But Mr Ashmore insisted the project was not yet finished, telling the BBC "touch-ups" were still needed.

"I usually use a scissor lift, where you can stand back and see things as a whole, but I couldn't use it as the land is too uneven," he told the BBC.

"I saw people saying it looks like Michael Jackson or a zombie.

"I've got thick skin, I'll be okay, but it didn't feel fair."

On Friday, scaffolding was back up at the mural, which is on a wall some two miles from the Crucible, where the World Championships take place each year.

articles.title: Bugatti desnuda al brutal Bolide y crea el Destrier, una escultura única de 1.600 CV
articles.standfirst: El Destrier es una pieza única de apenas un metro de altura que conserva el W16 de 8,0 litros y cuatro turbos, pero cambia la obsesión por la aerodinámica por la elegancia.
articles.summary: El Destrier es una pieza única de apenas un metro de altura que conserva el W16 de 8,0 litros y cuatro turbos, pero cambia la obsesión por la aerodinámica por la elegancia.
articles.body: El Bugatti Bolide nació como un hypercar extremo, concebido con una única obsesión: conseguir las máximas prestaciones posibles dentro de un circuito. Un coche de competición explícito y sin concesiones, cubierto de alerones y soluciones aerodinámicas destinadas a generar carga para pegarlo al suelo. Pero ¿qué sucedería si se eliminara todo aquello y quedaran al descubierto únicamente sus extraordinarias proporciones? Esa es la pregunta que Bugatti ha respondido con el Destrier, una creación única que parte del chasis del Bolide, pero que desemboca en un deportivo escultural, sin extremismos. El resultado es un coche que conserva la base técnica y mecánica de la máquina de circuitos, pero que sustituye su agresividad visual por una carrocería mucho más limpia y elegante. Todo ello sin renunciar al monumental motor W16 de 8,0 litros, cuatro turbos y 1.600 CV tan característico de los hypercar franceses. El Destrier tiene, además, otro atractivo: es único. Se trata de la tercera pieza surgida del Programme Solitaire, el departamento de Bugatti dedicado a crear los vehículos más especiales para sus clientes más especiales. Así surgieron primero el Brouillard y el F.K.P. Hommage, ambos con el pasado como punto de partida. Pero en el Destrier la marca francesa ha optado por volcarse en el diseño. El nombre del superdeportivo procede del término utilizado para denominar a los caballos más fuertes y valiosos empleados por los caballeros medievales. Una referencia que Bugatti ha trasladado tanto a la postura del vehículo como a varios detalles de su acabado. Uno de los rasgos más llamativos del Destrier es su escasísima altura: apenas un metro. Es sensiblemente más bajo que cualquier otro Bugatti y eso hace que parezca que su habitáculo está encajado entre las dos aletas delanteras. La carrocería se estrecha de forma muy marcada por detrás de las puertas y vuelve a ensancharse sobre las ruedas posteriores, simulando la cintura y las caderas humanas. Su postura recuerda, según Bugatti, a la de un caballo poderoso preparado para abalanzarse sobre su objetivo. En las llantas vemos otra diferencia respecto al Bolide, que utilizaba ruedas de 18 pulgadas, mientras que el Destrier descarga su aspecto con unas de 20 pulgadas delante y 21 detrás, que parecen todavía más grandes debido a la reducida altura de la carrocería. Su identidad se construye desde el momento en el que Bugatti decide deshacerse de los elementos aerodinámicos que radicalizan el aspecto del Bolide. En su lugar aparecen superficies limpias, formas suaves y una interpretación diferente de algunos de los rasgos estéticos modernos de la marca. Por ejemplo, la característica línea en forma de C de la zona acristalada deja de ser un trazo ininterrumpido porque ahora conecta con la parrilla delantera que, aquí sí, mantiene su característica forma de herradura… aunque en el Destrier es de mayor tamaño. En la parte posterior el alerón se integra en la propia silueta, una solución que recuerda a la utilizada por el exclusivo Chiron Profilée. La dualidad que representan el Bolide y el Destrier ya se ha dado antes en Bugatti con el Type 57 y sus derivados de competición (Type 57G y 57C Tank) que incluso ganaron en Le Mans a finales de los 30, y con el Type 57SC Atlantic, considerado uno de los automóviles más bellos de todos los tiempos. De hecho… esa relación se plasma en un detalle del Destrier: una placa grabada mediante láser sobre el parabrisas donde aparecen el Type 57G Tank y el Type 57SC Atlantic, dejando constancia de esa relación entre competición y elegancia. Un coche de la máxima exclusividad tenía que cubrirse con algo especial. Por eso, la pintura del Bugatti Destrier está terminada en un color denominado Sapphire Celeste, desarrollado específicamente para esta unidad y para su propietario. Se trata de una pintura multicapa con partículas inspiradas en el brillo de los diamantes, combinada con diferentes elementos de aluminio pulido. Hay algunas partes desnudas, como el splitter delantero y al difusor trasero, que mantienen la fibra de carbono a la vista, aunque teñidas para integrarse con el particular tono azul de la carrocería. Otro detalle particular lo encontramos en el vano motor, donde algunos componentes metálicos presentan un acabado martillado que recuerda a las armaduras fabricadas artesanalmente para los caballeros medievales. Una alusión directa al origen del nombre Destrier. Donde cualquier referencia al Bolide desaparece es en el interior… como es lógico. El cockpit de carreras da paso a un interior que Bugatti compara con el taller de un sastre. La cabina combina cuero y nubuck en el tono marrón Ambre Voyageur con un tejido tridimensional elaborado mediante técnicas procedentes de la alta costura y de la ropa deportiva. Es un tejido sin costuras visibles pero que está atravesado por finos hilos de cobre que aportan pequeños destellos. Su diseño forma una especie de halo que recorre el interior y se reproduce en los reposacabezas y en las líneas de la consola central. El acabado metálico martillado del vano motor que mencionábamos antes también aparece en los tiradores de las puertas, las salidas de ventilación, el centro del volante y las placas de acceso. Hay una pequeña bandera francesa para recordar el origen de Bugatti y la guinda la pone el tapón de llenado de aceite, que incorpora el emblema del Destrier junto a la inscripción “1/1”, que certifica que no existirá otro automóvil igual. Ante todas estas delicatesen de diseño, el extraordinario motor W16 de 8,0 litros con cuatro turbocompresores y 1.600 CV pasa casi a ser un detalle secundario. Algo quizá lógico cuando lo importante no es la lucha contra el reloj ni los tiempos por vuelta en pista. El protagonismo es para a sus proporciones, los materiales empleados y el trabajo artesanal. De ahí que su puesta de largo mundial tuviese lugar en uno de los mayores eventos del planeta automovilístico, la Monterey Car Week que culmina con el famoso Concurso de Elegancia de Pebble Beach. Su precio no ha sido comunicado (y quizá nunca llegue a saberse), aunque tratándose de una pieza única del Programme Solitaire, probablemente sea uno de los automóviles nuevos más caros jamás construidos.

articles.title: David Cantero, plata en las Series Mundiales de Weihai tras una caída
articles.standfirst: En una jornada de lluvia intensa, el español fue segundo tras el suizo Max Studer, que revalidó la victoria del pasado año
articles.summary: En una jornada de lluvia intensa, el español fue segundo tras el suizo Max Studer, que revalidó la victoria del pasado año
articles.body: El español David Cantero ha logrado la medalla de plata en la prueba de las Series Mundiales de triatlón disputada en Weihai (China), donde revalidó la victoria del pasado año el suizo Max Studer. El helvético, que participaba en su primera prueba este curso, cruzó la meta en solitario después de una actuación sólida bajo la lluvia en un crono de 1.41:08, mientras que Cantero retornó a un podio desde Wollongong el año anterior y el bronce fue para el canadiense Tyler Mislawchuk. Tras una intensa prueba de natación, la lluvia obligó a los participantes a ser cautelosos en el sector de bicicleta, con lo que se formó un grupo en cabeza con 28 triatletas, entre ellos Cantero y Alberto González y el resto de favoritos. El australiano Matt Hauser, vigente campeón mundial, fue uno de los que se cayó durante el recorrido, pero ello no le impidió llegar al tramo de carrera a pie junto al resto de aspirantes. Abrió hueco rápido junto al japonés Kenji Nener, Cantero, Studer y Mislawchuk, aunque estos tres últimos tomaron el mando en la segunda vuelta y dejaron atrás a sus compañeros del grupo cabecero. Poco a poco fueron incrementando su ventaja y en la tercera vuelta una caída complicó la carrera a Cantero. Studer aprovechó esta circunstancia para atacar de nuevo y el español no pudo aspirar a la victoria, pero al menos pudo alejarse de Mislawchuk para certificar la plata a diez segundos del vencedor. "Estoy muy contento de volver al podio. La carrera de hoy fue una locura, un día lluvioso, y tuvimos que tener mucho cuidado. Todos querían estar al frente, pero yo me concentré en mantenerme a salvo. En la carrera a pie tuve una pequeña caída y perdí mi último impulso, pero aun así logré llegar al podio, así que estoy muy contento, sobre todo porque hoy la carrera a pie fue muy táctica y no es a lo que estoy acostumbrado. Suelo ir a tope porque vengo desde atrás, pero hoy estaba al frente, así que tuve que ser muy táctico, y funcionó", explicó Cantero. Mientras tanto, Alberto González acabó en la novena posición con un crono de 1.42:08, Izan Edo decimocuarto con 1.42:44 y Roberto Sánchez Mantecón vigésimo quinto con 1.43:54. En la prueba femenina se impuso la francesa Cassandre Beaugrand con 1.49:20, por delante de la británica Beth Potter (1.49:26) y de la alemana Lisa Tertsch (1.49:44). Sara Guerrero finalizó vigésima tercera con un tiempo de 1.53:41.

articles.title: World Triathlon Championship Series: Cassandre Beaugrand wins again in Weihai with Beth Potter second
articles.summary: France's Cassandre Beaugrand earns her fourth straight win in the World Triathlon Championship Series as Britain's Beth Potter comes second in Weihai.
articles.body:
France's Cassandre Beaugrand earned her fourth straight win in the World Triathlon Championship Series as Britain's Beth Potter came second in Weihai.

Olympic champion Beaugrand surged away in the final kilometre of the 10km run to finish in one minute 49.20 seconds and maintain her perfect record in this season's Championship Series.

Beaugrand's victory in China followed a thrilling tussle up until the final stretch, as Olympic bronze medalist Potter finished six seconds behind the 29-year-old.

Germany's Lisa Tertsch was third, a further 18 seconds back.

"This one was definitely not easy," said Beaugrand.

"I was feeling great on the swim, great on the bike. The run was quite hard with Beth pushing the pace. I just tried my best to keep up and trust my finish."

Beaugrand exited the two-lap 1500m swim in third behind Britain's Tilly Anema and Brazil's Vittoria Lopez.

After a close bike section, where a pack of more than 30 cyclists merged together at the front, Beaugrand, Potter and Tertsch started to break away on foot.

On the final lap as Tertsch started to fade away, Potter fought valiantly but she could not keep in touch with Beaugrand's searing pace.

Beaugrand's victory means she has overtaken Potter, despite competing in fewer races this year, to go top of the World Triathlon Championship Series standings.

The men's race was won by Switzerland's Max Studer, who finished in 1:41:08.

Spain's David Cantero del Campo finished 10 seconds behind, with Canada's Tyler Mislawchuk in third, a further seven seconds back.

There is one more regular-season event in the Czech Republic on 13 September, before the Grand Final in Spain on 23 September.

articles.title: Chelsea vs Brighton: Premier League – preview, team news, prediction
articles.summary: Brighton will fancy their chances against Chelsea though, having won their last three league games against the Blues.
articles.body:
Who: Chelsea vs Brighton What: English Premier League Where: Stamford Bridge, London, United Kingdom When: Sunday, August 30, at 2pm (13:00 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 10:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Chelsea and Brighton will look to build on decent starts to the season, as the Blues welcome the Seagulls to Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea began life under new coach Xabi Alonso with a breathless 3-2 victory at West London neighbours Fulham in the Premier League on Monday as their exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer all found the net.

They then followed that up with a solid 2-0 win over Luton in the League Cup on Thursday.

But Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton side also came into the game in a buoyant mood after recording back-to-back 4-0 home wins over Aston Villa in their Premier League opener last weekend and against Norwegian side Tromso in a Europa Conference League playoff on Thursday.

Brighton will also fancy their chances against Chelsea, having won their last three league games against the Blues while finding the net three times on each occasion.

Fernandez’s Chelsea future uncertain as Alonso seeks commitment

Alonso said he wants players that “feel a desire” to play for Chelsea after Enzo Fernandez was left out of Thursday’s League Cup win over Luton.

The Argentina midfielder has been linked with a move to Manchester City, but no suitor has yet met Chelsea’s reported 120 million-pound ($162m) valuation of Fernandez.

The 25-year-old came off the bench in the Blues’s 3-2 win over Fulham to give Alonso a winning start to his reign in the Premier League on Monday.

However, the former Real Madrid boss hinted that Fernandez may not be involved against Brighton.

“We need to take everything into consideration: players that are in good moments, players that are not feeling that energy to play. For me, it’s very important that they feel that desire to play and to have good preparation,” said Alonso.

“We talked and we decided that [for Luton] it was better not to be part of the squad. He’s a top player, there’s no doubt about that.”

Selling Fernandez would ease the pressure on Chelsea to meet financial sustainability regulations after another window of heavy investment in the transfer market.

Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Marco Palestra, Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria, Danny Welbeck, Emmanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda have arrived at Stamford Bridge for combined fees in excess of 300 million pounds ($406m).

Aston Villa’s Emiliano Martinez is also set to join to replace the error-prone Robert Sanchez as Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper.

There have also been a number of departures from the club in recent days, including strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson.

Alonso, who previously said his bloated squad size needed to be drastically cut, is satisfied with the clear-out.

“We are quite close to the plan that we had. We will see where we finish, if it’s fully executed or there are some things still to be done,” he added.

“But overall the balance of what we have is going to be good. We need to see how the last few days develop.”

After a poor season, Palmer looked back to his best against Fulham as he thrived while roaming in a free role under Alonso.

During his pre-match news conference, Hurzeler warned his side cannot defend against Palmer on a “one-to-one” basis and must be collectively strong to stop the playmaker and Chelsea’s other talents.

The German coach said he was happy with his own squad as the transfer window is set to close.

“There’s a minor issue with small injuries but I’m not here to complain; I’m here to find solutions together with my team and that’s what we try to do since day one, so yes, I’m happy with the squad,” he said.

He said new signings Jaouen Hadjam and Promise David should be available for the Chelsea game.

I think they are two great players. Two great personalities. They make our squad stronger,” he said.

The Opta supercomputer has made Chelsea the favourites, with a win probability of 49.6 percent. Brighton were given a 26 percent chance of winning, while a draw was estimated at a 24.4 percent likelihood.

The two clubs have faced each other 28 times, with Chelsea winning 16 games, Brighton winning 7, and five matches ending as draws.

Brighton have won the last four encounters between the two sides, with Chelsea’s last victory in the tie coming back in September 2024.

April 21, 2026: Brighton 3-0 Chelsea (Premier League)

September 27, 2025: Chelsea 1-3 Brighton (Premier League)

February 14, 2025: Brighton 3-0 Chelsea (Premier League)

February 08, 2025: Brighton 2-1 Chelsea (FA Cup fourth round)

September 28, 2024: Chelsea 4-2 Brighton (Premier League)

What happened the last time the two clubs met?

Brighton’s Ferdi Kadioglu netted an early opener, and Jack Hinshelwood and Danny Welbeck scored in the second half to pile more misery on floundering Chelsea in a 3-0 Premier League victory back in April.

The result saw Brighton climb above their visitors to sixth in the table, with Chelsea in the midst of a dire run of results that would see them miss out on European football this season.

Marco Palestra remains unavailable with an injury, as is Jordan Henderson, who continues to recover from a broken wrist sustained while celebrating England’s last-16 World Cup win over Mexico.

However, Alonso said he was hopeful that key midfielder Moises Caicedo will be fit enough to face his former club, while Levi Colwill and Geovany Quenda are also in contention to play.

Defender Wesley Fofana returns after serving his suspension for a red card on the final day of last season at Sunderland.

Alonso suggested that the unsettled Enzo Fernandez may not feature as he is being linked with a move to Manchester City.

Yankuba Minteh, Kaoru Mitoma, Stefanos Tzimas and Evan Ferguson are all long-term absentees for Brighton.

Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter are doubts after picking up knocks. If Rutter is unable to feature, then either Charalampos Kostoulas or new loan signing Promise David could start up front.

articles.summary: Will Sharman, plata en los Juegos de la Commonwealth, su hermano Richard Sharman y Lamin Deen también fueron condenados pero habían abandonado ya Marruecos
articles.body: Tres exdeportistas británicos fueron condenados en Marruecos en el marco de una investigación sobre la agresión sexual a una menor por parte de un entrenador de velocidad, según adelantó BBC Sport. La investigación judicial llevó al ingreso en prisión de Leon Baptiste, técnico de atletismo del Reino Unido y oro en los 200 metros en los Juegos de la Commonwealth de 2010. Así lo confirmó entonces una fuente del ministerio de Justicia marroquí. Baptiste fue arrestado en mayo por una agresión sexual a una menor y se encuentra recluido en el centro penitenciario de Oudaya. Ahora, las sentencias judiciales a las que ha tenido acceso BBC Sport desvelan que Will Sharman, dos veces medallista de plata en los Juegos de la Commonwealth en vallas, su hermano Richard Sharman y Lamin Deen, ambos exdeportistas de bobsleigh, que estaban de vacaciones con Baptiste, fueron declarados culpables de participar en la incitación a un menor. Sin embargo, ellos no fueron detenidos y han conocido sus condenas por la prensa: penas de prisión suspendidas de cuatro meses. Abandonaron Marruecos creyendo haber cumplido con todos los requisitos que se les impusieron. "En aquel momento, entendieron que habían pagado una multa administrativa equivalente a aproximadamente 40 libras esterlinas y que el asunto había concluido", aseguran desde su entorno Según la sentencia, "ayudaron (a Baptiste) a engañar a la menor y a persuadirla para que mantuviera relaciones sexuales (con él). Esto constituye participación en la incitación a una menor".

articles.title: El olímpico Heath Ryan, sancionado 18 meses por maltrato animal
articles.standfirst: Se había publicado en redes un vídeo que mostraba al jinete azotando repetidamente a un caballo
articles.summary: Se había publicado en redes un vídeo que mostraba al jinete azotando repetidamente a un caballo
articles.body: El jinete olímpico australiano Heath Ryan ha sido suspendido durante 18 meses y multado por el organismo rector mundial de la equitación tras una investigación sobre acusaciones de maltrato animal. El jinete de doma clásica y concurso completo ya había sido suspendido por la Federación australiana el año pasado después de que un vídeo que parecía mostrar a Ryan azotando repetidamente a un caballo se publicara en las redes sociales. La Federación Ecuestre Internacional (FEI) impuso el viernes esta suspensión al jinete, de 68 años, alegando que había desprestigiado el deporte e infringido el código de conducta de la FEI en materia de bienestar animal. "El Tribunal de la FEI concluyó que Ryan incurrió en maltrato animal de conformidad con el artículo 142.1 del Reglamento General de la FEI, lo que desacreditó tanto a la FEI como al deporte ecuestre", aseguró en un comunicado Ryan, que compitió por Australia en doma clásica en los Juegos Olímpicos de Pekín 2008, también fue multado con 3000 francos suizos (5174 dólares) y se le ordenó pagar la misma cantidad para sufragar los gastos legales de la FEI. Su sanción tiene carácter retroactivo, así que concluirá el próximo diciembre. No es la primera vez que un jinete o amazona recibe una sanción tras comprobarse que ha existido maltrato animal. La amazona británica Charlotte Dujardin fue expulsada de los Juegos de París tras filtrarse un vídeo de años atrás, en el que la amazona entrenaba a un joven jinete golpeando hasta en 24 ocasiones en menos de un minuto a su caballo. La amazona emitió entonces un comunicado en el que aseguró que "lo que ocurrió fue completamente fuera de lo común y no refleja cómo entreno a mis caballos ni cómo preparo a mis alumnos, pero no hay excusa. Me siento profundamente avergonzada".

articles.body:
Rafael Leao is flying out to Istanbul to undergo his medical tests with Galatasaray: 'Thanks for everything, ' he said before leaving. ' I've felt at home since day one.'

Portuguese winger Leao is ready to join Galatasaray. Last night, he was at San Siro for Milan's 2-0 loss against Venezia, but was not available and spoke to journalists after the final whistle.

JAKARTA, INDONESIA – AUGUST 08: Rafael Leao of AC Milan shoots against Moises Caicedo of Chelsea FC during the pre-season friendly between Chelsea FC and AC Milan at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia. (Photo by Peksi Cahyo/Getty Images)

A few hours later, he packed his luggage and prepared for his trip to Turkey, where he'll join Galatasaray on a permanent deal exceeding €45m.

"I wanted to be on the field, say goodbye to the fans and feel their energy, but it wasn't possible," he told reporters.

"I wish Milan the best; I'll keep watching them from afar. That's how life goes. A cycle is over, and a new one begins. I'm happy to start a new adventure in a new country, in a team that is doing really well," he continued.

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 24: Rafael Leao of AC Milan looks on from the substitutes bench prior to the Serie A match between AC Milan and Cagliari Calcio at the Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 24, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Talking about his next club, Galatasaray, Leao added: "Last season, they showed what they can do in the Champions League. It's a very important competition for me too. We'll play against great European clubs, so the target is to add quality to their team, which already has strong players."

He also sent a message to Milan fans: "Thanks for everything. I've felt at home since day one. Every time my family came to visit me, they also felt at home, so I only have to thank them. I was very happy to wear their shirt. We won important trophies, and surely I'll always carry Milan in my heart."

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 10: Rafael Leao of AC Milan gestures during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Atalanta BC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 10, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Lastly, a reporter asked if criticism from the media made Leao upset in recent years, but he replied with a smile: "Many times, but this is how things go. This happens in life: when things go well, everyone speaks well; if not, it's right that people talk, but if they talk, it means you have something different."

Some of those cuts are beginning Aug. 29. But it's more than just cutting players. There are possible trades as teams try to move a surplus at one position in exchange for needed depth at another.

For the Eagles, that could involve trading one of their backup quarterback candidates in Tanner McKee or Andy Dalton. It could even involve trading a linebacker, perhaps Jeremiah Trotter Jr., who's good enough to start for many teams. After all, Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio called that position the deepest on the defense.

Either way, the Eagles need to pare down the roster by 37 players. They have had a full training camp, with two joint practices against the Patriots, and three preseason games to make their evaluations.

It's not necessarily the best 53 players who'll make the roster. After all, it's possible that football newbies Uar Bernard and Joshua Weru, both signed through the International Player Pathway program, will make the roster even though they never played organized football before this summer.

But the Eagles might have to keep them because they could get claimed on waivers if not. That, in turn, will affect some other players, such as a veteran like wide receiver Elijah Moore.

articles.title: Pakistan white-ball coach Mike Hesson to join England tour amid disastrous Test series performance: Report
articles.summary: Pakistan white-ball coach Mike Hesson is set to join the national squad in England early following severe batting collapses in the Test series, according to...
articles.body:
Mike Hesson will join Pakistan's Test squad in England as their batting collapse deepens under head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed.

Ollie Robinson and Jofra Archer combined for seven wickets, bowling Pakistan out for just 110 at Lord's.

Sarfaraz admitted his batters aren't spending enough time at the crease, despite England's lead ballooning to 261 runs.

SOS in England! Pakistan to fly in white-ball coach Mike Hesson to rescue disastrous Test tour

Pakistan's Test crisis in England has grown serious enough to prompt a fresh intervention, with white-ball head coach Mike Hesson reportedly set to travel and join the squad as their fortunes continue to unravel at Lord's.

England seized firm control of the second Test, building a commanding 261-run lead by the end of day two.

Ollie Robinson and Jofra Archer did most of the damage, sharing seven wickets between them as Pakistan folded for just 110 in their first innings, with a deficit of 180 runs. Adding to Pakistan's woes, opener Imam-ul-Haq couldn't bat at all after straining his calf while fielding on the opening day.

Shan Masood stepped in to open in Imam's absence and edged behind after failing to handle a full delivery clocked at a brisk 146kph. Abdullah Shafique's ordeal began just as roughly, as he was greeted with a 92mph bouncer on his very first ball that struck him on the hand as he ducked for cover.

Captain Babar Azam, back in the side after missing the opener through injury, managed only 8 before edging Josh Tongue behind to Jordan Cox at third slip. Robinson then removed both Saud Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan lbw on review, either side of a brief rain interruption.

With Imam unable to bat at all, Pakistan's innings ended after just 37.2 overs, with just 110 runs on the board.

Now, according to Geo News, Hesson will fly out and join the team in England to help steady a side that's badly lost its way in the longer format.

What did Sarfaraz Ahmed say about Pakistan's batting struggles?

Pakistan coach Sarfaraz Ahmed didn't shy away from addressing the batting collapse directly, admitting the team's inability to occupy the crease has become a recurring problem.

"See, you can't shy away from the fact that our team is getting bowled out in 30 or 35 overs," Sarfaraz said.

"Obviously we have discussed this and the batters also have an idea about the fact that we are not spending enough time on the pitch.

"Yes, conditions are definitely challenging for the batters but whichever batter spends more time in the middle and plays 30 to 40 balls [will benefit]. The first 30-40 balls are difficult but if we can get past that, we will be in a better position."

He was also asked whether Pakistan's heavy focus on T20 cricket over the past year, driven by the Asia Cup and T20 World Cup, had contributed to their red-ball struggles. While acknowledging it as a factor, he stopped short of using it as an excuse.

"It is a big factor. Last year, we played nearly 40 or 50 T20 games. But I won't say that is the reason - as professional players, we need to adjust [between formats]," he said.

Despite England's commanding 261-run lead on a pitch that's clearly favoured bowlers throughout, Sarfaraz insisted he hadn't given up hope of a turnaround. "I am still hopeful. A lot of unexpected things happen in cricket. If we can bowl them out within the next 70-80 runs and chase a target under 350, you never know," he said.

Could Mike Hesson eventually take over as Test head coach?

Bringing in Hesson mid-series raises an obvious question about whether this arrangement could evolve into something more permanent, particularly given how badly Pakistan's red-ball fortunes have deteriorated under Sarfaraz.

Hesson brings serious international coaching pedigree, having previously guided New Zealand to sustained success, and his tactical experience could help Pakistan address some of the batting fragility on display at Lord's.

That said, replacing Sarfaraz feels premature based on this series alone. Test batting collapses often stem from deeper structural issues, technique, domestic pitch conditions, and format overload, rather than purely coaching shortcomings, and Sarfaraz himself acknowledged as much. Bringing Hesson in as additional support makes sense as an immediate fix, but a full coaching change mid-crisis risks looking reactive rather than strategic.

If Pakistan's batting struggles persist beyond this series, though, a serious conversation about restructuring the coaching setup, potentially with Hesson taking a bigger red-ball role, would become far more justified. For now, treating this as reinforcement rather than replacement seems the more sensible path, giving Sarfaraz room to address the issues he's already identified before any bigger decisions get made.
