articles.title: The annual frenzy of NFL transactions happens this weekend
articles.summary: Rosters must cut from 90 to 53 by Sunday at 4:00 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
The Turk will be very busy this weekend.

The traditional name for the in-house harbinger of doom, each team's Turk will be telling players on the bubble that the coach wants to see them.

"And bring your playbook," he usually adds.

It's one of the basic realities of a sport that has 90 players on the roster until the limit plunges, in one fell swoop, to 53. And it will happen through an avalanche of moves that will trim the rosters, build practice squads of up to 16 players, and then spark a flurry of additional cuts and signings at the bottom of the roster.

The process is the most basic reminder of the reality that the supply of willing NFL players far outweighs the demand. And that, once the preseason ends, the demand for players to play in the games that don't count instantly evaporates.

Players who are released with four or more years of service instantly become free agents. Players who aren't "vested veterans" migrate to the waivers system.

Any team can claim a player on waivers, with no limit on the number taken. The players are awarded by priority based on the 2026 draft order, with the Raiders having dibs on all of them.

This means that players who make the 53-man roster as of Sunday at 4:00 p.m. ET may not be around for long. For every player claimed on waivers, another player needs to be removed from the roster.

The roster cuts at one point were made on the Saturday of Labor Day weekend, only five days before the first game. When the season moved to 17 games, the process was accelerated by a week or so, giving the players who make the team a break before Week 1 preparations begin in earnest.

The deadline had been Tuesday. This year, the decision to move the first game to the Wednesday after Labor Day (with two teams heading to Australia for a game the next day) prompted a shift to Sunday.

All in all, it's a harsh process. The teams largely have become desensitized to it, because it's a fundamental step in building a team. And the players who don't have starting jobs set in stone understand that there's a risk they'll be leaving their current teams, possibly temporarily. Possibly for good.

The practice squad helps to soften the blow. And those 16 spots for 32 teams create up to 512 more jobs.

The churning of the roster and the practice squad will continue, throughout the regular season and into the playoffs. The availability of short-term injured reserve will create opportunities. Players who aren't attached to a team will get tryouts.

For those who don't make it to a 53-man roster, the dream isn't dead. It's in limbo. And many of them will choose to stay in shape and wait for the phone to ring.

articles.title: Maynard pens new Ashland book
articles.summary: Writers write about what they know. One of the area’s best storytellers has penned another informative tale about 11 players who have stood the test of time,...
articles.body:
One of the area's best storytellers has penned another informative tale about 11 players who have stood the test of time, and one of the most cherished rosters in the rich Ashland football history.

Mark Maynard, former editor and longtime sportswriter for The Daily Independent and current managing editor of Kentucky Today, releases a new book next month titled "The Boys They Called JAWS."

It's a deeper, more detailed story about a beloved Tomcats team, a fierce defense and an unforgettable season.

Maynard believes a book can offer more than a well-crafted article or feature. The pages offer a rousing chance to reminisce and relive memories still talked about today.

"It's not news, it's reacting to something that's happened," Maynard said. "I think it's important to give some of the background that people don't know. I've only written one fiction book. Everything else has been about things people may already know, and generally they know that Ashland's 1975 team was called JAWS. Why were they called JAWS? Not everybody knows that, and it has some other neat things that happened during that time."

Maynard graduated from Ashland in 1975 and became great friends with many on the vaunted Ashland defense that dominated the gridiron the following fall. The Tomcats would win 14 games that season, tied for the most with the 1990 state champions.

The 1975 Cats earned the at-large state championship. Due to unfortunate timing, a thrilling road playoff win at Paducah did not come with a Class 3A title. In February of that year, the Board of Control for the Kentucky High School Athletic Association met and implemented a four-class system for football. The champion from the Louisville area would meet the at-large champion in a winner-take-all scenario.

It was the first season in which any Louisville school played a team from outside Jefferson County for a state title.

St. Xavier, a private school, wore down the Tomcats in the second half on its home field, using a massive roster and constant substitutions on both offense and defense. Ashland gave the Tigers their toughest test of the season. The Tomcats only trailed 6-0 at halftime before falling for the only time that year, 20-0.

"I grew up with those guys," Maynard said. "I knew many of them very well. I have written a ton about them throughout my time at The Daily Independent. I interviewed (former coach) Herb Conley in podcasts, and I have a lot of fresh quotes from him that people have never heard. I went back and got more information from the newspapers and writers who covered them at the time.

"They know what happened, but people may not know everything about them," he added. "I hope that they will pick this book up and go through it and see what an amazing season that was and how good they were."

The JAWS nickname originated after Conley and family attended the famous JAWS movie over a summer vacation. Ashland was enjoying one of its most successful stretches during Conley's tenure, and a defining description of his defense could add extra motivation and reignite the physicality of a team that didn't make the playoffs the previous year.

"Herb knew they could be really good," Maynard recalled. "The other coaches were into it. They talked to the team and told them they were thinking about it. The team wanted to do it. Of course, 18-year-olds would want that nickname. Herb told them that they need to live up to it. If you do this, you need to live up to it. They proved it early in the season. They didn't give them the name until they upset No. 1 Bryan Station in the second week of the season. They did it with defense. After that, it took off. They just annihilated people. The offense was good too. It wasn't solely built on defense."

Maynard said the personal connection to the team was the main reason he wrote the book. He also knew the team's connection to the community. The players bleed maroon. They grew up on their streets. They were friends with their kids. They called Ashland home.

"The team holds special memories for me," Maynard said. "They were a bunch of fun guys. They weren't prima donnas or anything like that at all. They were respected. They were all Ashland kids. There were no recruits or transfers that came in to help them. They were Ashland kids, and that made it more special. It's why the community wrapped their arms around them. They loved them. They had the band play the JAWS theme when the defense came on the field. The place was packed every Friday night."

The postseason included a long cross-state trip to Paducah for the at-large state championship. It would be a six-hour bus ride, but the town had other plans. The community raised money for a Southern Airways flight so they could arrive for the biggest game of the season in just 60 minutes.

Maynard has many of these stories inside the new book. It speaks highly of a group and a team that people are still talking about them a half century later.

"This team did a lot of firsts," Maynard said. "It was a fun book to write, and it was fun to revisit those games again. I had been planning to write this book for 10 years. The team was adored in Ashland.

"I have thought so much about this book for so many years that the words just came out," he added. " I knew the games, and I knew what had happened. We have stats in the back of the book. The cover has the iconic picture of that team. I really enjoyed writing it. I have written so many stories, but books have a different excitement. You try to make it as perfect as can be."

"The Boys They Call JAWS" will be released in late September. Readers can preorder a softback or hardback edition of the book. The link can be found on Maynard's Facebook page.
authors: Matt Sparks, The Daily Independent, Ashland, Ky.

articles.title: Cricketers vs footballers: Indian team owner stirs debate with ‘cooler,’ 'fitter' athlete claim
articles.summary: Ranjit Bajaj has sparked a massive online debate by claiming football players are far fitter and cooler than cricketers.
articles.body:
Delhi FC owner Ranjit Bajaj sparked debate by claiming average footballers are fitter and cooler than average cricketers.

Bajaj previously challenged Virat Kohli's fitness, saying his U13 academy players beat the Indian cricketer's recorded Yo-Yo test score.

He explained the contrast through muscle physiology, comparing football's instinctive reflexes to cricket's more predictive waiting game.

'Footballers are fitter & cooler!' Indian football club owner sparks massive firestorm with attack on cricketers' fitness

A fresh sporting debate has taken hold across Indian sports circles, pitting cricket's celebrated fitness culture against football's demanding physical grind, and it's a club owner known for blunt opinions who's stirred the pot once again.

Comparing athletes across different sports is nothing new. Fans have always enjoyed these arguments, but things get heated whenever someone claims one discipline produces categorically superior athletes.

That's exactly what's happened here, thanks to some provocative comments from Ranjit Bajaj, Minerva boss, as he weighed in on stamina, style, and overall athleticism.

In an interaction with sports presenter Ridhima Pathak, the conversation took a lighter but still argumentative turn when Pathak asked whether footballers carry a cooler image than cricketers. Bajaj didn't hesitate in linking overall fitness directly to aesthetic appeal.

Pathak asked: "Do you guys also feel that footballers are cooler than cricketers?"

Bajaj hit it straight out of the park and said: "Yeah, yeah, man. Let's see. What about you? What do you think?"

Pathak didn't want to commit, and Bajaj doubled down on her and said: "No, no, you're... you are the perfect person to be asking this because you... No, no, you've put you on the spot. So what do, what do girls think? Who is cooler, the footballers or the cricketers?"

Pathak still didn't want to commit and reluctantly said: "I'll have to ask the girls."

Bajaj then went on a rant and explained: "See, so I can say it openly, man. A normal average footballer will be much fitter than a normal average cricketer, by far. By far, okay? So if girls like fit men, and it's the same thing...

"I'm not generalizing and I'm not saying they can't be fit. There are people like Virat Kohli who is super fit. There are a lot of cricketers who I've seen, like Shubman, my boy, he's really, really fit and he takes pride in that. The new generation, yes."

One must note that this is not unfamiliar territory for Bajaj, as he had earlier claimed that his U-13 boys at Minerva have a better Yo-Yo score than Kohli.

Bajaj explains the physiological differences between athletes of the two sports

Bajaj went further, breaking down how differing muscle demands and reaction speeds shape each sport's athletic requirements.

"In football, you use muscles which are fast-twitch muscles, and there is no time to make decision-making," he said.

"It has to be natural because of the number of times you've done it in your life before," he explained, using Lionel Messi as an example of instinctive, split-second movement rather than conscious deliberation.

He then contrasted that with cricket's more anticipatory nature.

"In cricket, you know the ball is going to come, it's going to come, and then you're going to smash it," he said.

"Now you are waiting for the ball, it's going to come, you know it's going to come in this area. You're waiting. Yes, fast-twitch muscles are used right in the end when the reflex is there. But before that, you know your first movement towards the ball and like that is because of where the ball is pitched."

An interesting theory, but the comparison oversimplifies both sports

Bajaj's physiological breakdown makes for compelling conversation, but it flattens two different athletic disciplines into a single fitness hierarchy that doesn't hold up.

Football certainly demands sustained cardiovascular endurance across 90 minutes, but cricket, particularly fast bowling and modern fielding standards, requires its own brutal combination of explosive power, repeated sprinting, and injury resilience that rarely gets the credit it deserves.

Using average athletes from each sport as the comparison point also feels like a shaky foundation for such a sweeping claim, since fitness standards vary wildly within any sport depending on level, role, and era. Comparing elite youth academy trainees to a national cricket team's general fitness baseline isn't exactly an apples-to-apples measure either.

articles.title: UNH football opens season with 28-14 loss at UAlbany
articles.summary: Brooks Bentley threw for 230 yards and two touchdowns, but UNH football opened its season with a 28-14 loss to UAlbany on Friday.
articles.body:
ALBANY, N.Y. — Senior quarterback Brooks Bentley threw for 230 yards and two touchdowns, but the University of New Hampshire football team fell to UAlbany, 28-14, on Friday at Bob Ford Field at Tom and Mary Casey Stadium.

Senior wide receiver Ja'Carree Kelly led the Wildcats' receiving corps with six catches for 123 yards, including a 45-yard touchdown reception. Myles Thomason paced the ground game with 53 rushing yards and also caught a 4-yard touchdown pass.

Defensively, sophomore linebacker Trevor Barry recorded a career-high 13 tackles, while sophomore safety Cohen Cook added 10 stops. Darren Burton II also came up with an interception for UNH.

On the first possession of the game, Burton II intercepted Colón's pass at the UAlbany 45 to give the ball to the Wildcats.

UNH, on the opening drive, took advantage of an Albany personal foul on a 37-yard field goal attempt that extended the drive. Bentley lofted a pass to the left flat corralled by Thomason at the 8-yard line and he ran into the end zone at 8:07 for the first score of the season. Lucas Glassburn kicked the PAT to give the 'Cats a 7-0 lead.

Trailing 21-7, it took UNH only two plays to cover 74 yards in 37 seconds to trim the deficit at 14:21 of the third quarter. Thomason ran around the left end for a 29-yard gain to the UAlbany 45, then Bentley connected with Kelly in stride down the middle of the field for a 45-yard touchdown.

The Wildcats return to action on Saturday, Sept. 5, when they travel to face Syracuse.

articles.title: Adil Aouchiche expected to extend Schalke stay until 2030
articles.summary: FC Schalke 04 no longer have to worry about the future of Adil Aouchiche, with the midfielder set to stay in Gelsenkirchen long term.As reported by Sky Germa...
articles.body:
FC Schalke 04 no longer have to worry about the future of Adil Aouchiche, with the midfielder set to stay in Gelsenkirchen long term.

articles.title: BS Meter on Latest AEW All In Rumors, New WWE's Bloodline Plans, Drew McIntyre's Return, More
articles.summary: Pro wrestling itself might be heading for what one could consider a mini-offseason in the post-SummerSlam haze before things really kick up after the holidays into WrestleMania prep.
articles.body:
Pro wrestling itself might be heading for what one could consider a mini-offseason in the post-SummerSlam haze before things really kick up after the holidays into WrestleMania prep.

The buzz just keeps on flowing in a major way around the sport. This week features Roman Reigns and Bloodline speculation around WrestleMania plans, major names swapping companies and how big debuts change things.

And that's just a small hint. To help fans keep up with the rumor mill, let's throw the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

The Drew McIntyre speculation should end soon. According to PW Insider (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), he's ready to come back, but WWE creative doesn't have anything for him right now.

It's no secret McIntyre had outside commitments. Fans last saw him in April and probably best remember his brief title win over Cody Rhodes, only to give it right back. Whether that was due to his needing to take a break or not remains unknown.

This all tracks. McIntyre wasn't involved at SummerSlam, so he always figured to be back in the fall at the earliest. And with how fluid things are on a weekly basis, it's not a shock that WWE creative wasn't holding something for him. Expect him soon, though.

The most recent episode of Raw featured a major surprise: The OTM debut. According to False Finish (h/t Mrosko ), those inside WWE liked how things went over for the stable as they got involved with Bloodline stuff.

This was a weird one. A brutal live crowd that was pretty silent for most of the Raw broadcast didn't have much of a reaction to the major debut. But the internet was ablaze about it, and thankfully, it sounds like WWE internally aligns with the internet on this one.

There have been disastrous debuts in the past that made it super-obvious those behind the curtains wouldn't be happy. OTM aligning with Royce Keys and making things interesting with Solo Sikoa-LA Knight-Bloodline stuff was the opposite as a fantastic surprise.

It's still just a matter of time, right? According to WrestleVotes (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), the expectation remains that New Day will debut in AEW at All In.

New Day at Wembley Stadium? Sounds fun. Xavier Woods and Kofi Kingston feel like a matter of time in the promotion after the shocking WWE release. And as speculated by most, them popping up in the trios gauntlet match seems like the obvious landing spot, at least initially

It will never not be weird to consider Xavier Woods and Kofi Kingston as non-WWE-lifers. Alas, here we are. The biggest question isn't if the duo will go to AEW, it's when and by what exact name. All In was always the most obvious projected date.

Following buzz that Ilja Dragunov didn't want to be in WWE anymore, WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ) reports that AEW's Tony Khan will target him soon.

The report even mentions that perhaps Khan has already done so, if not signed Dragunov outright. When Dragunov suddenly left WWE, it was only a matter of time before this buzz started up.

Dragunov going to AEW is obvious. We'll see, though, if he's a bigger draw there, as WWE clearly didn't view him as a main-event guy who moves the proverbial needle. But it sure feels like he fits better over there, anyway. Maybe there's an outside chance he's another All In surprise?

What's next and for how long for The Bloodline? According to WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ), the plan for the current ongoing saga is to stretch through next year's WrestleMania. And for what it's worth, Wrestling Observer Radio's Dave Meltzer (h/t Knight ), suggested that The Rock might not happen due to money reasons.

First of all, no Rock involvement isn't that big of a surprise given his recent WWE flops and then absence. Second, the Bloodline continuing for that long would in no way be a shock, either, considering this new arc feels like it's just getting started. Fans haven't even seen Zilla Fatu involved just yet.

Easiest buy of the week. Why would WWE cut this saga off after Survivor Series? While there have been some dips at times, it's one of the best modern pro wrestling stories ever. Roman Reigns is top dog, the faction as a whole is interesting right now and Solo Sikoa is turning into a breakout star. No reason to earmark a premature end date, especially when the stories can build up to something really special with payoffs at WrestleMania.

articles.title: WWE's Cheat Code to Keeping Oba Femi Over
articles.summary: It's not often WWE strikes apparent generational gold as it has with Oba Femi.
articles.body:
It's not often WWE strikes apparent generational gold as it has with Oba Femi.

It is often, though, that WWE struggles to keep a popular star hot for an extended period of time. No matter how good things seem right now, it's a valid concern.

But WWE has a cheat code to avoid any mistakes with Oba Femi:

Word is, according to PW Insider (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), that McIntyre is ready to return to WWE, but that the company's creative doesn't have anything for him yet.

Maybe they're just waiting for Femi to get done with Bron Breakker.

There have been plenty of justified questions about just how WWE can keep Femi interesting and fresh all the way up to next year's WrestleMani. He's very much earmarked for Roman Reigns at that event, barring a shocker. But it's a long time away, especially in the land of pro wrestling.

Make no mistake, WWE is right to do Femi-Breakker right now. It's a money feud, in part, because Femi really did take Breakker's spot while the latter was out injured. There's no better story to tell than one that has so many real-life truisms and perhaps no better way to really kick start the next generation.

But presuming Femi-Breakker isn't a super long feud, which it probably shouldn't be so that Breakker can go win a Money in the Bank or find his own 'Mania direction, McIntyre is a genius opponent for Femi.

Think about it. McIntyre is amazing as a heel foil. He's great on the mic. Physically, he's imposing enough to look like a serious threat to Femi. And storyline-wise, he's got plenty of reason to aim at a top dog in the main-event scene who…also happened to take down Brock Lesnar in spectacular fashion.

Fans have seen him take part in major, long-running feuds, too. Remember how long his feud with CM Punk stretched? That was a feat on its own, with McIntyre feuding with an injured guy and still making it fresh and entertaining on a weekly basis.

The alternatives aren't all that great, either. What is Femi going to do after Breakker? There's not exactly a long list of part-time legends he can run through anymore. Guys like Randy Orton and Seth Rollins have their own things going on and somebody like LA Knight might not be able to afford another loss.

Granted, Femi will eventually head to Bloodline land, no doubt, in order to start setting the foundation for the feud with Reigns. But not right away. And that faction, with Solo Sikoa booming and new stables getting in the mix, seems to be heading its own way for a good long while yet.

No, McIntyre is by far the most logical next step. He deserves something fresh too, as opposed to coming back and getting in the mix with Rhodes or Punk or something random like Gunther. Returning and seeing that he's been a bit shoved aside for a new thing like Femi, too, makes for a compelling motivation.

McIntyre, by the way, can afford a loss. Absorb it, even, better than most of the roster. His iconic comeback story to WWE, then putting the company on his back during the audience-less era, is something that will never go forgotten. Eventually losing a memorable feud to Femi? Just another high mark on the resume.

One could argue that Femi doesn't need help staying over with fans. But as the above hints, this is just as much about protecting the rest of the roster as it is preserving Femi's over-ness with fans.

McIntyre has morphed into an all-timer of a modern great over the years and his unique set of abilities, the Lesnar link and everything else make him the perfect extended main-event program situation for Femi.

Everyone should be able to see that easily enough. And most would probably agree that, despite a predictable outcome, the Femi-McIntyre back-and-forth would be important viewing each week.

For WWE, anything should be on the table to preserve what they've stumbled upon with Femi. McIntyre, though? He makes it head-smackingly obvious and easy. Everybody wins, including fans.

The Detroit Tigers dropped the weekend home series opener to the Los Angeles Dodgers on Friday night, 2-1. Tarik Skubal threw six frames of one-run ball for the visitors, but that was all the offense would score, leaving no room for error for the relief corps — and of course with this group, there is always a hiccup or two.

Taking the mound for the Tigers on Saturday afternoon looking to even the series is right-hander Keider Montero, who has produced mixed results in his seven games since returning to the starting role. Cumulatively, the 26-year-old has put up a solid 3.22 ERA along with a 4.46 FIP, but three of those outings saw him get tagged for three or more runs, resulting in all three of his losses over that stretch.

Most recently, Montero gave up three runs on four hits (one home run) and a walk while striking out three Pittsburgh Pirates in a 4-1 loss at PNC Park.

For the Dodgers, left-hander Blake Snell will make his fifth start of the season after missing three months following surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow. The 33-year-old was roughed up in his first appearance of 2026, but since then has thrown three straight six-inning quality starts, posting a microscopic 1.00 ERA along with an impressive 2.08 FIP on seven hits and walks while striking out 21, along with a hit-by-pitch and a wild pitch.

One of the top returning small-school runners in the state, Monroe's Aiden Koroush won the 3A/2A/1A Special District 2 title last season with a personal-best 5,000 time of 16:40.5. He ended the year with the 15th-fastest time in Oregon among 2A/1A runners.

Only 14 boys in the state, regardless of classification, clocked a faster 5,000 time than North Eugene's Ashenafi McKinnis did during his junior season.

McKinnis ended 2025 with a personal-best of 14:55.4. He also had a stellar track and field season, placing sixth at the Class 5A state championships in the 3,000 and 10th in the 1,500.

Siuslaw rising junior Bentley Nelson ran a 5,000 personal best of 15:50.8 last fall — eighth-fastest in the state among Class 3A boys.

Nelson placed 12th at the 3A state championship meet.

During a breakout sophomore year, South Eugene's Khalil Sabzalian produced his best performances during the championship portion of the season.

Sabzalian placed fourth at the Southwest Conference district meet, 21st at the Class 6A state championships and ended his campaign with a personal-best time of 15:23.8 at the NXR Northwest Regional Championships.

The reigning Class 4A state champion will look to add another title to his resume this fall.

Marist Catholic rising senior Corbin Sage won the 2025 cross-country title in thrilling fashion and finished the fall with a 5,000 personal-best of 15:24.6.

In the spring, he doubled up on titles, winning the 1,500 state championship. The Spartans' versatile star also placed second in the 3,000.

As a sophomore last season, Cottage Grove's Remington Sharkey ran the 28th-fastest 5,000 time in Class 4A. He clocked a personal-best 16:52.9 at the Sky-Em League Championships to finish third before going on to place 27th at the 4A state meet.

One of the more accomplished distance runners in recent state history, South Eugene senior Yosuke Shibata spent his junior year establishing himself as one of the top prep distance runners in the U.S.

Shibata won the Class 6A state cross-country championship in the fall and captured the 1,500 state title during the spring track and field season.

Following his XC state title, he placed fourth at the NXR Northwest Regional Championships and earned a highly coveted trip to NXN Nike Cross Nationals, where he finished 23rd in a field featuring the nation's best high school runners.

Early in his sophomore season, Siuslaw's Henry Stone ran a massive 5,000 personal best of 15:24.0, which ranked third among Class 3A boys in 2025. Stone placed fourth at the 3A state championship meet.

In the spring, he was the Class 3A runner-up at 3,000 meters and ended the season with a personal-best time of 8:42.07.

articles.title: Lightning delay does little to slow Alamo Heights in rout of Pieper in season opener
articles.summary: The Mules opened the Texas high school football season with a three-hour rain delay, but they showed no signs of slowing down in a win over Pieper.
articles.body:
The thunderstorm that made its way through the San Antonio area wasn't the only semblance of lightning at Pieper Warrior Stadium on Friday night.

Alamo Heights scored on its first two possessions and the Mules' quick-strike offense was only slowed by a three-hour weather delay in a 43-14 victory over Pieper in their season opener.

Quarterback Easton Stone and receiver Charlie Mitchell sparked the Mules as they connected for three touchdowns. Stone threw for 190 yards and four scores, with Mitchell catching scoring passes of 24, 25 and 2 yards. He finished with five catches for 53 yards.

Stone's last scoring toss went to Landon Balldin on a 73-yarder in the third quarter, accounting for most of the latter's 103 yards receiving on five catches.

It was Mitchell's first taste of the sport in high school as the basketball player came out for the football team for the first time this season.

"I'm blessed honestly," Mitchell said. "Easton has been throwing me perfect balls, and I just couldn't be more grateful to my coach, everything and all the work I've put in. I was always playing basketball all my life, and I didn't want to go to college regretting that I wouldn't play high school (football). So, I just decided I would go out and try it. So, I'm really happy out here.

"Me and Easton, we've been working on the field since 5 a.m. to late nights. It's always the chemistry," Mitchell added. "I was already friends with Easton before I started playing football, and I think that correlates. We've put in a lot of work, a lot of reps. It goes along way."

The rout of Pieper was a good way to start the Rudy Nerio era at Alamo Heights. Nerio takes over for Ron Rittimann, who retired after spending the last six seasons leading Alamo Heights.

"We talk about controlling the controllables and not worrying about things like weather, and things like that and our guys have really bought in to what we're selling," Nerio said. "Unbelievably proud of how they started, how they responded after a weather delay and all the credit goes to our guys."

Nerio was pleased with the start Mitchell had in his debut football game.

"What an awesome debut today," Nerio said. "Super excited about Easton (Stone) and the leadership he brings at that position at quarterback. I'm excited to see how that connection keeps growing."

William Bishop capped a quick, five-play opening drive with a 40-yard touchdown run, powering his way into the end zone to put Alamo Heights up 7-0 with 9:32 left in the first quarter.

Lee Brockwell intercepted Pieper quarterback Chase Lyons near midfield to set up Alamo Heights' next score. Stone then connected with Mitchell on his first scoring pass, a 24-yarder on a fade route to put the Mules up 13-0 with 8:22 remaining in the first after the point after kick was missed.

Officials delayed the game late in the first quarter because of thunderstorms in the area. Play resumed around 10:30 p.m., with the game ending early Saturday morning.

The duo of Stone and Mitchell continued where it left off following the delay, as Stone found Mitchell open up the middle on a 25-yard catch-and-run and a two-yard scoring toss in the second quarter.

In between the two Mitchell touchdown catches, Wade Springer gave Pieper a glimpse of hope when he bolted on a 54-yard scoring run in the second quarter to get the Warriors within 20-7. Stone and Mitchell then answered the Pieper score with their two-yard scoring connection, and then Will Trevino had a pick six for the Mules, going 34 yards on an interception return to give Alamo Heights a 33-7 halftime lead.

Lyons finished with 216 yards and two scores, including a 65-yard touchdown pass to Luke Jordan, but the Alamo Heights defense pressured him into throwing four interceptions and sacked him twice.

Alamo Heights racked up 374 yards of total offense while Pieper managed 312 total yards in defeat.

It was the first meeting between the two schools since Pieper defeated Alamo Heights 53-46 in the Class 5A Division II regional semifinal playoff in 2023.

The game was a rough start for new Pieper coach Eddie Salas, who took over the reins of the team after Nick Rogers stepped down after last season. It was also Pieper's first game as a Class 6A program after playing their first five years in Class 5A.
